A.explanation: Starts at $4.0\text{ V}$ at X and falls linearly to $2.0\text{ V}$ at Y, matching the p.d. from slider to the bottom wire.

B.explanation: Starts at zero and rises, which would measure from X downwards instead of from the slider to the bottom common point.

C.explanation: Falls to zero at Y, which ignores the $10\text{ }\Omega$ fixed resistor Q still between Y and the bottom wire.

D.explanation: Rises from $2.0\text{ V}$, which is the reverse trend - the resistance from slider to bottom decreases as the slider moves X to Y.

hints: Notice where the two voltmeter leads go: one to the slider on P and one to the bottom wire common with Q and the battery.
Think of the voltmeter reading as the p.d. across Q plus the p.d. across the lower part of P from the slider to Y.
Calculate the series current with total $20\text{ }\Omega$ and then find $V$ at X with $20\text{ }\Omega$ below the top, and at Y with only $10\text{ }\Omega$ below the slider.
walkthrough: Identify the loop: P ($10\text{ }\Omega$) in series with Q ($10\text{ }\Omega$) across $4.0\text{ V}$, so total $R = 20\text{ }\Omega$ and current $I = V/R = 4.0/20 = 0.20\text{ A}$.
Identify what V measures: p.d. between the slider and the bottom node, so $V = I \times R_{\text{slider to bottom}}$.
At X the resistance below the top connection is full P plus Q: $R = 10 + 10 = 20\text{ }\Omega$, so $V = 0.20 \times 20 = 4.0\text{ V}$.
At Y the resistance below the slider is only Q: $R = 0 + 10 = 10\text{ }\Omega$, so $V = 0.20 \times 10 = 2.0\text{ V}$.
As the slider moves uniformly from X to Y, the lower resistance falls uniformly, so $V$ falls linearly from $4.0\text{ V}$ to $2.0\text{ V}$ and never reaches zero because of Q. This is option A
